changelog:
CSM 1.0.878

Fixes to the theming you reported

• On home and result cards the play badge no longer sits in a hard-edged dark
  square: CSM was stamping an opaque background over CloudStream's own
  translucent, rounded play/progress container. Those poster, play, progress,
  badge and chip overlays are now left exactly as CloudStream laid them out.
• Text on coloured surfaces CSM tints (accent buttons, filled chips, the home
  FAB) is now derived from the surface colour instead of staying white, so
  "Abspielen", "AniWorld" and similar labels stay readable on a light accent.
• The washed-out video is fixed. CSM's full-screen pause scrim, and the
  now-playing, speed and sleep-timer badges and the next-episode pill drawn over
  the picture, had been following your palette background colour, so a light
  palette painted a light veil over the whole frame. Overlays drawn on video now
  keep a palette-independent dark fill with their original alpha and corner
  radius; only their text and tint follow your theme.

Episode totals on cards (opt-in, off by default)

• "Show episode totals on native cards" can now also show the total where the
  provider did not report one: CSM asks CloudStream for that provider, loads that
  single series once and reads its real episode count. Nothing is guessed from
  progress, quality or title text.
• Bounded and quiet: at most two loads at a time, at most four per screen pass,
  identical cards are coalesced, results are cached for ten minutes and failures
  suppressed for a minute, only visible attached cards with a series type start a
  load, and a late answer can never land on a recycled card.
• The setting text discloses that this loads each series once and uses extra data.

Sharing and import

• Fixed a real defect in CSM's own write gate: the process-wide mutation lease was
  released only after a main-thread resumption that does not always arrive,
  leaving the gate permanently busy. That could silently block clearing protected
  history, where the PIN dialog never appeared, and make a settings import commit
  nothing. The lease is now released on the thread that runs the blocking write.

Appearance coverage

• Your CSM theme reaches the rest of CSM: player controls and overlays, minibar,
  sleep timer, speed lock, subtitle and effect panels, the built-in keyboard, home
  and result cards, the sources panel, side panel, toolbar, search, settings
  pages, CSM dialogs, notifications, the debug overlay, the view inspector and the
  home-layout editor.
• Changing the palette updates those surfaces right away, and turning CSM off puts
  the host colours back exactly as they were.
• Kept deliberately: score and age-rating tiers, quality and language labels,
  notification type accents, download-progress and destructive states, the black
  video dimming layer, the translucent-white surfaces with black stateful icons,
  and the dark video-scrim action buttons.

Discord

• The Discord sign-in dialog now looks native: the page sits in a rounded host
  card with clipped corners and a matching background, the title stays on one line
  with the close button beside it, and the subtitle is a single ellipsised line.
• Sign-in behaviour is unchanged: same allowlist, mixed-content blocking,
  progress, error and Retry handling, and the same session-token handling.

Notes

• CloudStream's own screens keep using CloudStream's own theme system. CSM cannot
  repaint those views: their colours are literal resources (the player's Sperren,
  Skalieren and Quelle buttons, the back button and "Intro überspringen" are
  transparent @style/VideoButton views with white text) and the Compose screens
  build their own Material theme. That was verified with tests rather than
  assumed; the CSM-owned surfaces are the ones that follow your palette.
• Nothing about sign-in, sharing, downloads or playback behaviour was changed
  beyond the write-gate fix described above.
